top_story_title: Cisco Expressway CVE-2026-76466 exploited in the wild days after PoC release; four devices breached
top_story_summary: Threat actors have exploited CVE-2026-76466 (CVSS 9.8), a critical flaw in Cisco Expressway, against a Russian organisation shortly after a proof-of-concept exploit was published. Reporting states four devices were breached and the attackers reached the internal network. The vulnerability allows an unauthenticated remote attacker with network access to the Expressway to compromise it.
top_actions: Inventory every Cisco Expressway (Expressway-C and Expressway-E) and record the running version; check it against Cisco's fixed-release table for CVE-2026-76466 - the public reporting does not state a fixed build, so use the vendor advisory.

Until patched, restrict inbound access to the Expressway at the upstream firewall to the source ranges that genuinely need it, and remove any administrative access (HTTPS admin, SSH, API) reachable from the internet.

Treat unpatched internet-facing units as suspect: review admin accounts, scheduled tasks, certificates and configuration for unexpected changes, and check logs for authentication anomalies around and after the PoC release date.
After upgrading, rotate local admin credentials, API tokens, certificates and any service-account secrets stored on the appliance, and terminate active sessions.
Queue the F5 work next: apply the BIG-IP hotfixes across every unit in each device group and verify config sync, and patch NGINX/NGINX Plus instances where HTTP/2 is enabled.
executive_summary: Cisco Expressway CVE-2026-76466 (CVSS 9.8) is being exploited in the wild after a public PoC; four devices were breached and the attackers reached the internal network. Patch per Cisco's advisory and treat exposed units as suspect.

F5 released emergency patches for five critical BIG-IP vulnerabilities (RCE and DoS) and five critical NGINX vulnerabilities, including two HTTP/2 flaws (CVE-2026-123007, CVE-2026-123633) fixed on 18 November 2026. No in-the-wild exploitation reported for either set.
SonicWall Generation 6 firewalls will receive no further security patches, including for critical flaws; the vendor says to retire them and get them off the internet edge immediately.

The OpenJDK flaw CVE-2026-114938 has produced portfolio advisories from both Cisco and Palo Alto Networks; both are rated at the top of their scales and neither collected advisory enumerates affected products yet, so track the vendor pages for product lists and fixed releases.
Two PHP RCE flaws (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) are in CISA KEV; they are not network-device bugs, but gateway IPS coverage is the stopgap for web stacks you cannot patch today.
No new defensive AI capability was announced by a network vendor in this window.
key_actions: **F5** — Pull the CVE list and fixed-version table from F5's advisory and compare against the running software version of every BIG-IP unit and vCMP guest.
**F5** — Apply the hotfix to all units in each device group and verify configuration sync afterwards; upgrade the standby member first and fail over.

**Cisco** — Locate every Expressway-C and Expressway-E, record running versions, and check them against Cisco's fixed-release table for CVE-2026-76466; schedule the upgrade immediately rather than in the next window.

**Cisco** — Before patching, limit inbound access at the upstream firewall to the source ranges that require traversal, and confirm no administrative service (HTTPS admin, SSH, API) is reachable from the internet.
**F5** — Inventory NGINX and NGINX Plus instances, including those embedded in appliances and container ingress, and record the running version against F5's fixed-release table.
**F5** — Prioritise instances that terminate internet-facing traffic and have HTTP/2 enabled; where patching has to wait, disabling HTTP/2 removes the exposure path described for the two HTTP/2 CVEs.
**Cisco** — Subscribe to or poll the advisory URL and recheck daily until the affected-product table is published; do not conclude you are unaffected from the current empty list.

**Cisco** — Build the candidate list now from your asset inventory: Cisco management, collaboration and monitoring products rather than switch and router NOS images, which are where bundled Java usually sits.

headlines.title: F5 releases emergency patches for critical BIG-IP RCE flaws
headlines.summary: F5 issued emergency patches for five critical BIG-IP vulnerabilities that can be exploited for denial of service or remote code execution.

headlines.title: Hackers Exploit Critical Cisco Expressway Flaw, Breach Four Devices and Reach Internal Network
headlines.summary: Attackers exploited Cisco Expressway flaw CVE-2026-76466 (CVSS 9.8) shortly after a PoC appeared, breaching four devices and reaching the internal network.

headlines.title: NGINX2Root: F5 patches five critical NGINX vulnerabilities
headlines.summary: F5 patched five critical NGINX flaws dubbed NGINX2Root that can reach remote code execution under certain conditions; no exploitation reported so far.

headlines.title: Vulnerability in Oracle OpenJDK (Java4Shell) Affecting Cisco Products: November 2026
headlines.summary: Cisco opened a portfolio advisory for the OpenJDK flaw CVE-2026-114938 (Java4Shell), an RCE triggered when processing Base64 content; affected products are not yet listed.

headlines.title: SonicWall Warns Gen 6 Firewalls Won't Get Security Patches, Even for Critical Flaws
headlines.summary: SonicWall says Generation 6 firewalls will get no security patches even for critical flaws, and tells customers to retire them and pull them off the internet edge now.

headlines.title: Two Critical NGINX HTTP/2 Flaws: What to Patch First
headlines.summary: Two critical NGINX HTTP/2 flaws, CVE-2026-123007 and CVE-2026-123633, allow takeover of the proxy without credentials when HTTP/2 is enabled; fixes shipped 18 November 2026.
